question: Must we verbalize the intention when giving sadaqah?
asked: When we give sadaqah, must we verbalize the intention? There are many types: fidya, kaffarah, sadaqah, zakah; which of them is the most beneficial? When I give, is money better or food better, or how about helping somebody out? What additional steps can we take to derive the most benefit out of charity? And when we give charity, can we intend something of this world as well from Allah, such as protecting myself from evil, curing a sick one or more wealth, or must we intend only the next? Is that going to harm the purity of the intention?
answer:
All of these questions, mashallah, deal with the reality of charity and how to maximize the impact of charity. And I want to just point out that, mashallah, our brother is really thinking deeply about this issue. You can tell he's deconstructing every single aspect, and he's eager to gain the maximum reward. And for me, inshaAllah, this demonstrates, inshaAllah ta'ala, a good heart. And it demonstrates that indeed our brother is upon the right path to get the maximum reward from Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Now, in terms of the specific questions he's asking. He says, must we verbalize the intention? And the response is that the verbalization of intentions is something that, generally speaking, the Sunnah has not come with. The only time that the Sunnah has come with verbalizing the intentions is when we go for Hajj. When we go for Hajj, we say "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk" out loud. And we make du'a to Allah: O Allah, make this Hajj or Umrah (both of them are the same in terms of verbalizing), make this a Hajj or Umrah in which there is no showing off, in which we are doing this for Your sake. And we say, O Allah, I am intending to do Hajj. O Allah, this is an Umrah for Your sake. O Allah, this is tamattu' or ifrad or qiran.

Otherwise, for every other deed that we do, the Shari'ah has not come with verbalizing the intentions. And therefore it is best to avoid doing this. There is no need to verbalize. Allah knows what is in your heart. Allah is the one who is 'Alim al-ghaybi wa al-shahadah.

And so I know some of our scholars and some of the madhhabs want you to verbalize, and they think that by verbalizing you are purifying your intentions and you're focused on what you're trying to do. I understand that philosophy. So they say, when you stand up to pray, say: O Allah, this is two raka'at for tahiyyat al-masjid, that's sunnah, that's for Your sake. O Allah, this is four raka'at, Salat al-Dhuhr. So you are focusing on the intention. I understand where they're coming from.

But of course the flip side is that you don't need to verbalize to focus on the intention. Allah knows your intention. You are standing up to pray Dhuhr or tahiyyat al-masjid, whatever it might be. **So there is no need to verbalize the intention for any deed. Allah knows your intention.** Yes, you must have the intention, but there's no need to verbalize it.
